daily.title: Hungary lifts PM Peter Magyar’s immunity, clears way for probes into 2 former Orban ministers
daily.summary: Prime Minister Peter Magyar has backed the move himself. Two former ministers who served under his rival Viktor Orban now face separate corruption probes.

daily.title: Pope decries 'scourge' of sexual abuse during France visit
daily.summary: French bishops took "courageous" steps when faced with "the painful scourge of abuse of minors," Pope Leo XIV told the high-ranking clerics before his scheduled meeting with survivors at the Catholic shrine of Lourdes.

daily.title: Turkey: Comedian on trial for 'insulting' Erdogan in show
daily.summary: Deniz Goktas is accused of "insulting" President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, "praising" crime and criminals, and "inciting hatred and hostility" with jokes about Islam. Nominally, Turkey is a secular country with free speech.

daily.title: Diesel prices are surging. Ukraine is only part of the story
daily.summary: Trucks, farms and industry are powered with diesel. Now prices are soaring due to refinery disruptions, supply shortages and geopolitical tensions. A potential US export ban could make Europe's diesel crunch even worse.

daily.title: Will Jürgen Klopp's charisma be enough for Germany?
daily.summary: After defeat to Greece, Jürgen Klopp is confronted with the real challenge of his task as Germany head coach. Can his charisma alone push this group forward?

daily.title: Ireland beat Israel 3-0 in Nations League match overshadowed by political controversy
daily.summary: Ireland easily beat Israel in a Nations League fixture that 24 hours earlier appeared in doubt. One Irish player pulled out of the match to express his opposition to Israel's actions in the Gaza Strip.

daily.title: Sweden faces political deadlock after election-winning center-left bloc fails to form government
daily.summary: Swedish Social Democratic Party leader Magdalena Andersson has abandoned efforts to form a four-party government. Deep divisions within the election-winning bloc have left Sweden in political deadlock.

daily.title: India: LPU suspends classes after violent protests over alleged campus rape
daily.summary: A university in Punjab has suspended classes after protests over a rumored sexual assault took a violent turn. Separately, the Supreme Court has taken suo motu cognizance of recent rape cases in Delhi. DW has more.

daily.title: Venezuelans demand opposition leader Machado's return
daily.summary: Hundreds of people held rallies in Venezuela demanding the safe return of Maria Corina Machado, and fair elections.

daily.title: Germany news: Berlin's Left files complaint against Dobrindt
daily.summary: Interior Minister Dobrindt could be in legal trouble after he seemed to accuse the Left's Elif Eralp of antisemitism. Domestic intelligence has warned on research cooperation with China. DW has more.

daily.title: What would Francis of Assisi make of his fame today?
daily.summary: The Catholic saint renounced wealth and fame to become a mendicant friar. Yet throughout history, his teachings and life have inspired popes, Dante and even Mussolini.

daily.title: Ukraine, South Korea relations sour over North Korean POWs
daily.summary: South Korea has accused Ukraine of breaching a confidentiality agreement over the transfer of North Korean prisoners of war — and of denying the deal's existence. Seoul has demanded an apology.

daily.title: Israel strips Dutch diplomats of status in West Bank
daily.summary: The move by the Israeli Foreign Ministry is a response to Dutch sanctions targeting goods from illegal Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank. The Dutch Foreign Ministry is yet to comment.

daily.title: Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic announces resignation
daily.summary: Aleksandar Vucic will now be running to be prime minister in the upcoming snap parliamentary elections slated for next month.

daily.title: Yemen: Houthis report deadly Saudi strikes on Taiz market
daily.summary: The Houthi-run health ministry accused the Saudi Air Force of committing an "abominable crime," vowing to retaliate. The Houthis' account of the attack cannot be independently verified.

daily.title: Avalanche in Nepal leaves 2 dead, several missing
daily.summary: An avalanche has struck the Himlung Himal base camp in Nepal after days of severe weather. Two guides are confirmed dead and at least 14 people remain missing in the remote region.

daily.title: UK: 5 arrested after 'major incident' near Fairford air base
daily.summary: Scores of homes were evacuated in the UK town of Whelford, near an air base used by the US military, with bomb disposal teams checking "suspicious vehicles" at the scene. Police said five men had been arrested.

daily.title: Two people killed as bus crashes on way to Oktoberfest
daily.summary: The bus was traveling from Italy to Munich, carrying 33 Filipino tourists who wanted to visit the famous beer festival. One of the dozens injured remains in life-threatening condition.

daily.title: European cities seek ways of boosting affordable housing
daily.summary: In many major urban centers of Europe, the housing shortage has become an explosive social issue. DW looks into various models that have been put in place across the continent.

weekly.title: Switzerland: Voters reject stricter view of neutrality
weekly.summary: Early projections show Swiss voters rejecting a stricter application of the country's vaunted neutrality. Swiss neutrality has been enshrined in the constitution since 1848.

weekly.title: Germany news: Are Germans giving up their beloved meat and sausages?
weekly.summary: Germans used to be all about sausages and meat. While those do remain popular, things seem to be slowly changing. There also are new insights into the economic side of East Germany's espionage DW has more.

weekly.title: Backlash over data centers tests Europe's AI ambitions
weekly.summary: Massive data centers needed to run AI are triggering protests across Europe. Their operators counter that they boost digital sovereignty and energy independence.

weekly.title: Russia expected to intensify hybrid war on Europe
weekly.summary: Drone explosions, airspace violations, arson attacks: Poland, Romania, and Moldova are now regularly targeted in Russian attacks against Ukraine. More governments are calling these attacks deliberate acts of aggression.

weekly.title: Russian students: Propaganda in school prepares them to die
weekly.summary: The Russian government wants children to learn about patriotism from an early age. DW spoke to students in Siberia about their views on propaganda at school on the war in Ukraine and their future.

weekly.title: DW shows solidarity with Georgians' commitment to democracy
weekly.summary: Cultural and media professionals in Georgia remain under threat. A DW panel brings together insiders who share their hopes and fears.

weekly.title: 'Lithuanian skies are NATO skies': DW speaks with Lithuanian premier Mindaugas Sinkevicius
weekly.summary: In a DW interview, Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevicius discussed threats to Lithuania from Russia and Belarus, NATO's need for stronger air defense and why military spending alone cannot ensure security.

weekly.title: Bundesliga, other top European leagues call for major FIFA reforms
weekly.summary: The Bundesliga and three other leading European football leagues have said major reforms to world-governing body FIFA are "essential." However, they stopped short of calling for the resignation of boss Gianni Infantino.

weekly.title: How Bulgaria become a global leader in battery storage and what this means for the country's grid and energy market?
weekly.summary: In under two years, Bulgaria has become one of the world's most battery-intensive energy markets. Can the surge last — and what will it mean for conventional power generators?

weekly.title: Italy to ban burqa in schools, limit foreign pupils
weekly.summary: Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni’s government has passed new school rules capping the number of students who don't speak fluent Italian and banning face coverings.

weekly.title: Jürgen Klopp starts Germany job with shaky Netherlands draw
weekly.summary: A late Netherlands goal denied Jürgen Klopp a win in his first match as Germany coach. The former Liverpool and Borussia Dortmund boss has big ambitions, but the game showed he's going to need more time to achieve them.

weekly.title: Three-way battle for power in world chess: Who will be elected FIDE president in Samarkand?
weekly.summary: The era of Russian presidents is coming to an end at the World Chess Federation (FIDE). Two Germans and one Kazakh are up for election. Among the issues at play are money, Kremlin influence, and unanswered questions.

weekly.title: After several difficult years, economists now expect German economy to grow
weekly.summary: Germany's economy is growing again, but recovery remains on shaky ground. High government spending is keeping the economy afloat, while energy prices, a shortage of skilled workers and debt continue to weigh on it.

weekly.title: Political psychology: Why extremist parties are thriving and what democratic politicians can do against it
weekly.summary: Far-right and far-left parties are celebrating success after success, leaving moderate politicians in the dust and worrying many Germans. Political psychology helps us understand what's behind growing polarization.

weekly.title: Could flattering AI make humanity turn on itself?
weekly.summary: A study shows chatbots mirror users' politics, part of a broader tendency known as AI sycophancy. Researchers fear this could deepen polarization.

weekly.title: Germany news: Berlin officially withdraws Olympics bid
weekly.summary: Berlin's decision to withdraw its Olympic bid means that only Munich and the western Rhine/Ruhr region are left in the running as potential Olympic hosts. DW has more.

weekly.title: Czech PM Andrej Babis reiterates importance of NATO for his country but rejects calls to increase defense spending
weekly.summary: The US and NATO want Czechia to spend more on defense. Czech Prime Minister Andrej Babis says Prague cannot afford faster increases, despite growing warnings about the threat from Russia.

weekly.title: 'Pope fever' takes hold as Pope Leo visits France
weekly.summary: Pope Leo XIV is expected to draw huge crowds during his visit to France. As part of his trip, he's also set to address Europe's future and some of the challenges ahead.

weekly.title: Could a Left Party government in Berlin expropriate large real estate companies?
weekly.summary: The socialist Left Party won the Berlin election partly on the promise to implement the city's 2021 expropriation referendum as a way to solve the city's rent crisis. But can it really happen?

weekly.title: China's 13-year-old swimming star raises questions on child athletes
weekly.summary: Three gold medals and three Asian Games records have catapulted China's Yu Zidi, 13, into the sporting spotlight. She is far from the first teen prodigy, but should teens be competing at elite level?

weekly.title: Slovakia: PM Robert Fico's NATO Article 5 remarks spark criticism and raise questions about his country's NATO commitment
weekly.summary: Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico says he fears war and will do everything he can to keep his country out of one. Critics say his remarks risk weakening NATO, the alliance that was designed to prevent such a war.

weekly.title: Germany's oldest party, the center-left SPD, is in a difficult position following its success in the Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania state election
weekly.summary: Chancellor Friedrich Merz (CDU) has vowed to press ahead with controversial reforms, but resistance is mounting within his coalition partner, the SPD. How much dissent can a governing coalition tolerate?

weekly.title: Munich and Cologne-Rhine-Ruhr – Germany's two remaining Olympic candidates
weekly.summary: Munich or the Cologne-Rhine-Ruhr region? Germany aims to host the Olympic Games again. Just two candidates are left after Berlin pulled out at the last minute.

weekly.title: El Nino explained: How the weather pattern affects hurricanes and tropical storms
weekly.summary: From drought to major floods and extreme heat, El Nino will have a huge impact on the world's weather. In the Atlantic, it could mean a season without hurricanes.

weekly.title: China's new travel rules unsettle tech giants and talent
weekly.summary: Beijing is locking the gates to stop expertise and capital in strategic industries from fleeing. The country accused of industrial-scale intellectual property theft now fears the West will take its own.

weekly.title: Famine threatens the Ukrainian town of Oleshky in the southern Kherson region as Russia delays creating a humanitarian evacuation corridor
weekly.summary: Food supplies to the town of Oleshky, in the occupied part of the southern Kherson region, have been cut off since May. Efforts by Kyiv to negotiate the evacuation of civilians with Moscow have been largely unsuccessful.

weekly.title: Germany news: Call to scrap once-a-day gas price rises
weekly.summary: The ADAC motoring association says a once-a-day rule on gas price changes has failed to help drivers' wallets. Entry-level jobs are becoming scarcer, making things hard for those entering the job market. DW has more.

weekly.title: Military aircraft crashes near US air base in Spangdahlem, Germany
weekly.summary: The F-16 pilot was able to safely eject from the plane and was taken to receive medical care. The incident occurred near Spangdahlem Air Base in the German state of Rhineland-Palatinate.

weekly.title: Young Berliners vote overwhelmingly for socialist Left  Party
weekly.summary: Berlin's young voters overwhelmingly supported the victorious socialist Left Party. Are the young more radical? Or are the election results just a reflection of current German politics?

weekly.title: Living in the shadow of LA's hidden oil wells
weekly.summary: Many lifelong residents of Los Angeles have health impacts from growing up close to oil extraction. Now, the city is trying to close down the worst offenders, but it's an enormous task.

weekly.title: Could we see MMA at the Olympics?
weekly.summary: Mixed martial arts has made its debut at the Asian Games this week. It takes the sport closer to the Olympics, but there are doubts about the next step — and the influence of the popular and lucrative UFC.

weekly.title: Male infertility is 'grossly underreported'
weekly.summary: It's not all on women anymore — doctors do test men for sperm count and motility. But still too few men get checked, possibly due to a misconception that a healthy sex life means healthy sperm. Spoiler: It doesn't.

weekly.title: 'Swan Song': New book by Princess Diana's brother drops
weekly.summary: A memoir penned by Charles Spencer on his older sister's life has been released, opening old royal wounds nearly three decades after Princess Diana's death.

weekly.title: Will Germany have enough gas this winter amid energy supply crunch?
weekly.summary: Germany's gas storage sites are far less full than in recent years. Officials say supplies are secure, but analysts warn that a cold winter or import disruptions could push prices higher. So how secure is the supply?

weekly.title: Germany news: VW to step up cost-cutting program
weekly.summary: Volkswagen's chief says the carmaker will accelerate its streamlining measures as workers protest. The Israeli ambassador says the Left Party win in Berlin polls poses a risk to the city's Jewish community. DW has more.

weekly.title: How will Germany's Merz respond after crushing state election results and losses to the far right?
weekly.summary: Germany's far-right AfD and the socialist Left Party gained ground in recent state elections, while the centrist parties lost support. The biggest loser is Chancellor Friedrich Merz.

weekly.title: Princess Diana's brother makes explosive claims about royals in new memoir
weekly.summary: Here are some of the key revelations from Charles Earl Spencer's highly anticipated memoir "Swan Song: Diana, My Sister." It has already provoked Buckingham Palace to react.

developing.title: India news: PM Modi says developing nations unfairly blamed for emissions
developing.summary: PM Narendra Modi has told a climate conference that developed countries emit six times more CO2 than India. Meanwhile, an IIT Bombay professor has been accused of caste abuse. DW has more.

developing.title: Live updates: Trump welcomes Xi to Washington
developing.summary: Donald Trump welcomes Xi Jinping to the US by greeting him personally at the tarmac at Joint Base Andrews. The two are expected to discuss trade, AI, Taiwan and Iran.
